findings.checklist_item: Scope `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` to be answered non-`na` only for the code-grounded cohort (as `asserted_capability_confirmed` does), or state in the plan/prompt that the field is answerable `yes` only when the verifier ran code-grounded — so the veto never fires on a tool-less verifier's ungrounded assertion.
evidence: Plan: 'set by the verifier via a present-state check: does the code AS IT IS NOW already satisfy the plan's directed end state?'
plan_review_grounding runs the AGENTIC verifier only when 'ANY Pass-1 finding cite[s] a CODEBASE_GROUNDED criterion (E4/G1G2/A1/G6)'; otherwise 'the cheaper single-turn verifier' with no code tools.

The R5 counterpart field asserted_capability_confirmed explicitly restricts non-na answers to the G6/E4/T3 cohort 'so it abstains from validity and never destabilises an existing review' (verify_models.py:66-88) — the plan states no analogous answering scope for the new field.
findings.finding: The veto trusts `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal="yes"` as a present-state fact, but the plan-review Pass-2 verifier only runs code-grounded (agentic, tool-equipped to inspect the current code) for findings citing a CODEBASE_GROUNDED criterion (E4/G1G2/A1/G6); a finding outside that cohort is verified single-turn without tools, so its `yes` is not a real present-state check yet would still fire the drop.
findings.location: Approach / Scope (verify_models.py new na-default binary; decide.py veto branch); cf. workflow_ops.py:272-289 plan_review_grounding and verify_models.py:66-88 asserted_capability_confirmed
scenarios: An execution-phase re-review of a finding whose criteria are NOT code-grounded, verified single-turn, where the tool-less verifier emits a confident but ungrounded `yes` — the finding is vetoed with no actual present-state inspection.
findings.suggested_fix: Document in the field description (and the two verifier prompts) that `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` stays `na` unless the finding is in the code-grounded cohort where the agentic verifier can actually inspect present code state, mirroring the asserted_capability_confirmed cohort restriction; add an AC/test that a non-grounded single-turn verification does not produce a definite `yes`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the present-state-check protocol per verifier variant: state that the non-tool-using single-turn verifier must answer current_state_satisfies_plan_goal="na" (abstain) when it cannot inspect current code, and that only the code-grounded agentic verifier may return a definite "yes".
evidence: plan_review_verifier.md front-matter is `execution_mode: single_turn` and lists NO repository tools; its body only says 're-ground in the plan (and, for code-grounded findings, the actual code)'.
Only plan_review_verifier_agentic.md exposes list_directory/search_files/read_file, and it is dispatched only 'when any Pass-1 finding is code-grounded'.
The plan directs documenting the field in BOTH prompt files but the single-turn variant cannot 'check the code as it is now' — the plan specifies no `na`/abstain fallback for that path.
findings.finding: The veto fires on a definite `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal="yes"`, which asserts the code AS IT IS NOW satisfies the plan's directed end state — a present-state CODE check — but the plan does not specify how the non-tool-using single-turn verifier is to perform that check, nor a fallback (e.g. answer `na`) when it has no code access.
findings.location: Scope bullet: plan_review_verifier.md / plan_review_verifier_agentic.md ('document the sub-answer'); Approach ('set by the verifier via a present-state check')
scenarios: A single-turn (non-agentic) plan-review verifier is asked to answer current_state_satisfies_plan_goal but has no code-reading tools; lacking a documented abstain rule it guesses `yes`, and under execution_review=True the finding is wrongly dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope/prompt-doc bullet, add the answer-setting rule: the agentic verifier sets "yes" only after confirming via read_file/search_files that current code already satisfies the plan's directed end state; the single-turn verifier defaults to "na" (never a definite "yes") since it has no code access.

findings.checklist_item: State, in the verifier prompt docs and the plan, the exact criterion the verifier applies to set current_state_satisfies_plan_goal='yes' (i.e. the code's present state affirmatively realizes the plan's directed end-state, distinguishing directed-and-done from never-needed/plan-wrong).
evidence: 'is set by the verifier via a present-state check: does the code AS IT IS NOW already satisfy the plan's directed end state?'
'without new history/intent inference' — but a present-state check alone cannot separate 'directed removal completed' from 'symbol was never present / plan is wrong'
The .md files are said to 'document the sub-answer' but the plan does not state the affirmative criterion the verifier uses to emit 'yes'
findings.finding: The plan specifies WHERE current_state_satisfies_plan_goal is set (the verifier via a 'present-state check') and WHEN the veto fires (execution_review AND definite 'yes'), but it does not state the CRITERION the verifier must apply to answer 'yes'. A bare present-state check ('does the code now satisfy the plan's directed end state') cannot by itself distinguish the intended case (the plan directed 'remove X' and X is correctly gone) from a genuine defect case (X is absent because the plan is wrong / the work was skipped). Without a stated answering protocol, the entire veto's correctness rests on an unspecified verifier judgment.
findings.location: Approach paragraph; plan_review_verifier.md / plan_review_verifier_agentic.md scope bullet
scenarios: Execution review where a Pass-1 finding is a TRUE positive (directed work skipped or plan references a symbol that legitimately should exist) but the verifier answers 'yes' because the present state happens to match some reading of the goal — a real defect is vetoed and a broken ticket closes
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach and both verifier .md updates a one-line answering rule: emit 'yes' ONLY when the plan explicitly directed the change AND the present code affirmatively matches that directed end-state; emit 'no'/'insufficient' when the discrepancy could reflect skipped work or a plan error.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the hard-veto (single-answer, outside GRADED_BINARY) choice against ADR-0032's rejection of vetoes for false-positive drops, or adopt the graded-validity axis it prefers.
evidence: docs/adr/0032-...md:43-46 `respects_artifact_altitude` is 'a graded validity input, not a veto ... rather than hard-vetoing (which would concentrate a fragile all-or-nothing judgement in one question)'

The cited a8e5 absence veto is a TWO-key refutation pair (decide.py:575 `claims_absence=='yes' and absence_confirmed_in_context=='no'`), not the single present-state 'yes' the plan proposes — the 'mirrors' claim is imperfect
Plan proposes `current_state_satisfies_plan_goal` OUTSIDE GRADED_BINARY so it 'never affects validity arithmetic' — the exact opposite of ADR-0032's chosen approach for a comparable FP
findings.finding: The plan chooses a single-binary hard veto for an execution-phase false-positive drop, but ADR-0032 deliberately rejected the hard-veto axis for a structurally identical false-positive (respects_artifact_altitude) in favor of a graded validity input, citing the fragility of concentrating an all-or-nothing judgement in one question; the plan does not engage this precedent or justify departing from it.
findings.location: Approach ('Add a single-answer Pass-2 VETO, mirroring the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto'); Scope bullet for verify_models.py (OUTSIDE GRADED_BINARY)
scenarios: A single mistaken 'yes' from the verifier drops a genuine execution-phase true positive at full validity/impact, with no arithmetic dampening — the fragility ADR-0032 warned about
Future maintainers cannot tell why altitude-FPs go on the validity axis while completed-work-FPs get a hard veto
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) cite ADR-0032 and argue why the completed-work FP warrants a hard veto where the altitude FP did not (e.g., it survives at validity 1.0), or (b) route the signal as a graded na-default validity sub-answer inside GRADED_BINARY so the arithmetic drops the FP, consistent with the established pattern.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a codebase-grounded rebuild-vs-extend rationale: explain why current_state_satisfies_plan_goal cannot be achieved by phase-gating the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto (decide.py:575) or the existing divergent_implementation='contradicts_reality' grade, and how the new binary avoids double-firing with them.
evidence: decide.py:575 — existing a8e5 veto already drops absence-premised findings: `if binary.get("claims_absence") == "yes" and binary.get("absence_confirmed_in_context") == "no"`
verify_models.py:240-254 — divergent_implementation='contradicts_reality' already grades 'a named symbol/file/behavior does not exist as described', which matches the plan's own motivating example

Plan Approach only asserts the new binary 'mirrors' a8e5 and does the check via 'a present-state check'; it does not enumerate why a8e5 or divergent_implementation cannot be phase-gated to the same effect (rebuild-vs-extend rationale absent)
findings.finding: The plan justifies a NEW third veto binary (current_state_satisfies_plan_goal) by analogy to the a8e5 absence-refuted veto, but does not ground WHY the existing overlapping mechanisms cannot be extended instead: the a8e5 pair (claims_absence/absence_confirmed_in_context in decide.py:575) already drops absence-premised findings, and the plan's motivating example ('the plan references X but no symbol X exists') is exactly what the existing divergent_implementation='contradicts_reality' grade (verify_models.py:240-254) already scores. A phase-gated drop keyed off the existing a8e5 pair or the divergent_implementation grade may capture the same false positive without a new binary.
findings.location: Approach section ('mirroring the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto'); Scope: verify_models.py binary_extra_fields
scenarios: A reviewer asks why a third veto binary is added rather than phase-gating the existing a8e5 absence-refuted veto that already targets absence-premised findings.

The new present-state check and the existing divergent_implementation='contradicts_reality' grade could double-fire on the identical 'plan references removed X' finding, creating two overlapping paths for one false-positive class.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, contrast the new binary's premise (present CODE state satisfies the directed end state) against a8e5's premise (plan CONTEXT contains a covering provision) and divergent_implementation (plan asserts a symbol that no longer exists), and state explicitly why neither existing signal can be phase-gated to cover the completed-work case — or fold the drop into one of them if it can.
